Factor correlation table

Source: R/loadings.R
apa_factor_cor.Rd

Makes an APA-style table of the correlations among factors (or components) from an obliquely rotated solution: a psych::fa() or psych::principal() object, or the output of parameters::factor_analysis() or parameters::principal_components(). For a lavaan model, the table shows the correlations among the latent variables in the fully standardized solution. When latent variables are linked by regression paths, these correlations are implied by the model.

Usage

apa_factor_cor(fit, factor_names = NULL, digits = 2)

Arguments

fit

a psych::fa, psych::principal, parameters::factor_analysis, parameters::principal_components, or lavaan object

factor_names

names for the factors. Either an unnamed character vector in the order the factors appear in the table (psych orders factors by variance explained), or a named vector that maps the original names to new names (e.g., c(PA1 = "Verbal")). The unnamed form is safer: after an oblimin rotation, the labels psych assigns (PA1, PA2, ...) can change from one run to the next, but the order of the factors does not.

digits

number of decimal places

Value

apa7_tbl (tibble)

Details

The factors are numbered in the first column, and the numbers are used as column headers. Only the lower triangle is shown. The factors are in the same order as in apa_loadings().

Examples

fit <- psych::fa(Harman74.cor$cov, 4, fm = "pa", rotate = "oblimin")
#> Loading required namespace: GPArotation
apa_factor_cor(
  fit,
  factor_names = c("Verbal", "Spatial", "Memory", "Speed")
)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 5
#>   Factor     `1`   `2`    `3`    `4`  
#>   <chr>      <chr> <chr>  <chr>  <chr>
#> 1 1. Verbal  —     ""     ""     ""   
#> 2 2. Spatial  .41  "—"    ""     ""   
#> 3 3. Memory   .30  " .27" "—"    ""   
#> 4 4. Speed    .40  " .38" " .32" "—"
